title: Paging backward across a chapter boundary opens the previous chapter at the start instead of the end
symptom: In page mode, tapping backward from the first page of a chapter jumped to the previous chapter's first page, which violated normal page-turn expectations.
root_cause: Cross-chapter backward navigation reused the default chapter-open path, and that path restores to chapter start unless an explicit restore-to-last-page intent is provided.
fix: Introduced boundary-aware chapter opening for page mode.
Mapped backward boundary turns to `restoreToLastPage` so the previous chapter opens near its last page instead of its start.
Added an instrumentation test for backward paging across chapter boundaries.
impact: The page-mode mental model broke at chapter edges, making paging feel inconsistent and unlike a real page-turn reader.
